Yes, the chance of high rainfall is smaller when observing waking up late.

To understand why, let's break down the given probabilities. We know that the probability of waking up on time and high rainfall is 53%, and the probability of waking up late and high rainfall is 8%. 

The key insight here is that we are comparing the joint probabilities of waking up on time and high rainfall versus waking up late and high rainfall. Since the probability of waking up on time and high rainfall is higher (53%) than the probability of waking up late and high rainfall (8%), it implies that waking up on time is associated with a higher probability of high rainfall.

In other words, when we observe that someone is waking up on time, we can infer that the probability of high rainfall is higher. Conversely, when we observe that someone is waking up late, the probability of high rainfall is lower.

This is an example of how conditional probabilities can be used to make inferences about the relationship between two events. In this case, the probability of high rainfall is conditional on the event of waking up on time, and the probability of waking up late serves as a counterfactual scenario.
